claim: The lateral-line neuromast of the zebrafish displays a restricted, consistent pattern of innervation that facilitates the comparison of microcircuits across individuals, developmental stages, and genotypes.
source: The lateral-line neuromast of the zebrafish displays a restricted, consistent pattern of innervation that facilitates the comparison of microcircuits across individuals, developmental stages, and genotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive SBFSEM analysis across multiple specimens described in the manuscript.

claim: Serial blockface scanning electron microscopy was used to determine from multiple specimens the neuromast connectome, a comprehensive set of connections between hair cells and afferent and efferent nerve fibers.
source: We used serial blockface scanning electron microscopy to determine from multiple specimens the neuromast connectome, a comprehensive set of connections between hair cells and afferent and efferent nerve fibers.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology and presents data from multiple specimens analyzed by SBFSEM.

claim: The neuromast connectome analysis delineated a complex but consistent wiring pattern with three striking characteristics: each nerve terminal is highly specific in receiving innervation from hair cells of a single directional sensitivity; the innervation is redundant; and the terminals manifest a hierarchy of dominance.
source: This analysis delineated a complex but consistent wiring pattern with three striking characteristics: each nerve terminal is highly specific in receiving innervation from hair cells of a single directional sensitivity; the innervation is redundant; and the terminals manifest a hierarchy of dominance.
evidence: The manuscript presents quantitative data and diagrams showing specificity, redundancy, and dominance across multiple specimens.

claim: Mutation of the canonical planar-cell-polarity gene vangl2 decouples the asymmetric phenotypes of sibling hair-cell pairs.
source: Mutation of the canonical planar-cell-polarity gene vangl2, which decouples the asymmetric phenotypes of sibling hair-cell pairs, results in randomly positioned, randomly oriented sibling cells that nonetheless retain specific wiring.
evidence: The manuscript presents SBFSEM data from trilobite mutants showing random hair cell orientations but preserved wiring specificity.

claim: In vangl2 mutants, randomly positioned, randomly oriented sibling cells nonetheless retain specific wiring.
source: Mutation of the canonical planar-cell-polarity gene vangl2, which decouples the asymmetric phenotypes of sibling hair-cell pairs, results in randomly positioned, randomly oriented sibling cells that nonetheless retain specific wiring.
evidence: The manuscript presents SBFSEM analysis of trilobite mutants demonstrating that sibling cells maintain distinct innervation patterns despite random positioning.

claim: Larvae that overexpress Notch exhibit uniformly oriented, uniformly innervating hair-cell siblings.
source: Because larvae that overexpress Notch exhibit uniformly oriented, uniformly innervating hair-cell siblings, wiring specificity is mediated by the Notch signaling pathway.
evidence: The manuscript presents SBFSEM data from Notch-overexpressing larvae showing uniform hair cell orientation and loss of wiring specificity.

claim: Wiring specificity is mediated by the Notch signaling pathway.
source: Because larvae that overexpress Notch exhibit uniformly oriented, uniformly innervating hair-cell siblings, wiring specificity is mediated by the Notch signaling pathway.
evidence: The manuscript presents data from Notch-overexpressing mutants showing loss of wiring specificity, supporting the role of Notch signaling.

claim: The assembly of the 10^15 synapses of the human brain is a formidable challenge that begins in the developing embryo.
source: The assembly of the 1015 synapses of the human brain is a formidable challenge that begins in the developing embryo.
evidence: This is a statement based on established neuroscience knowledge about brain development.

claim: Many neuronal connections form normally in the absence of activity, suggesting the presence of additional mechanisms guiding the targeting of synapses.
source: Environmental stimuli play a role in nervous-system development, but many neuronal connections nevertheless form normally in the absence of activity, suggesting the presence of additional mechanisms guiding the targeting of synapses.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in developmental neuroscience.

claim: The zebrafish's lateral line represents a simple but powerful model system for exploring the mechanisms that guide the assembly of microcircuits.
source: The zebrafish's lateral line represents a simple but powerful model system for exploring the mechanisms that guide the assembly of microcircuits.
evidence: This is supported by the comprehensive analysis presented in the manuscript and cited literature.

claim: Most fishes and many aquatic amphibians possess mechanoreceptive systems known as lateral lines.
source: Most fishes and many aquatic amphibians possess mechanoreceptive systems known as lateral lines, whose responsiveness to water currents underlies rheotaxis, predator avoidance, and schooling.
evidence: This is established knowledge about lateral line systems in aquatic vertebrates.

claim: The lateral line's responsiveness to water currents underlies rheotaxis, predator avoidance, and schooling.
source: Most fishes and many aquatic amphibians possess mechanoreceptive systems known as lateral lines, whose responsiveness to water currents underlies rheotaxis, predator avoidance, and schooling.
evidence: This is established knowledge about lateral line function supported by literature.

claim: Each lateral line consists of one to several neuromasts, which are discrete epithelial organs that include hair cells as well as the underlying supporting cells and surrounding mantle cells.
source: Each lateral line consists of one to several neuromasts, which are discrete epithelial organs that include hair cells as well as the underlying supporting cells and surrounding mantle cells.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about lateral line structure.

claim: Each hair cell possesses on its apical surface a mechanically sensitive hair bundle that is usually responsive to water movement either in the rostrad direction or in the caudad direction.
source: Each hair cell possesses on its apical surface a mechanically sensitive hair bundle that is usually responsive to water movement either in the rostrad direction—toward the animal's front end—or in the caudad direction—toward the rear end.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hair cell structure and function.

claim: Vectorial sensitivity results from morphological polarization of each hair bundle, which consists of an array of actin-filled stereocilia whose lengths increase progressively in the direction to which the bundle is responsive.
source: Vectorial sensitivity results from morphological polarization of each hair bundle, which consists of an array of actin-filled stereocilia whose lengths increase progressively in the direction to which the bundle is responsive.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hair bundle structure and mechanotransduction.

claim: In the larval zebrafish, directional responsiveness arises from differential innervation by two oppositely polarized subpopulations of hair cells.
source: In the larval zebrafish, directional responsiveness arises from differential innervation by two oppositely polarized subpopulations of hair cells, each attuned to the detection of water currents toward either the animal's front end or its rear end.
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in the manuscript and previous literature.

claim: During early development, the primary lateral line on each side of a larva comprises seven neuromasts.
source: During early development, the primary lateral line on each side of a larva comprises seven neuromasts, discrete organs each containing 8–20 hair cells that make synapses onto afferent axonal terminals and receive synaptic inputs from efferent terminals (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the schematic diagram in Figure 1A and established knowledge.

claim: Each neuromast contains 8–20 hair cells that make synapses onto afferent axonal terminals and receive synaptic inputs from efferent terminals.
source: During early development, the primary lateral line on each side of a larva comprises seven neuromasts, discrete organs each containing 8–20 hair cells that make synapses onto afferent axonal terminals and receive synaptic inputs from efferent terminals (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in the manuscript and Figure 1.

claim: In wild-type zebrafish there are approximately equivalent numbers of hair cells with hair bundles of the two polarities.
source: In wild-type zebrafish there are approximately equivalent numbers of hair cells with hair bundles of the two polarities (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by the fluorescence images and schematic diagrams in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Throughout the life of a fish, hair cells of the two types arise continually as transit-amplifying cells divide to produce sibling hair cells of opposing polarity.
source: Throughout the life of a fish, hair cells of the two types arise continually as transit-amplifying cells divide to produce sibling hair cells of opposing polarity (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Figure 1E and established knowledge about hair cell regeneration.

claim: The differentiation of new hair cells is mediated in part by lateral inhibition through the Notch signaling pathway.
source: The differentiation of new hair cells is mediated in part by lateral inhibition through the Notch signaling pathway (Lanford et al., 1999; Wibowo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on Notch signaling in hair cell development.

claim: Following mitosis, the newly formed sibling cells undergo a series of stereotypical rearrangements in their relative anteroposterior positions.
source: Following mitosis, the newly formed sibling cells undergo a series of stereotypical rearrangements in their relative anteroposterior positions, after which the more anteriorly positioned hair cell develops a hair bundle sensitive to caudad stimulation and the posteriorly positioned sibling extends a bundle responsive to rostrad water movement.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hair cell development in zebrafish lateral line.

claim: After rearrangement, the more anteriorly positioned hair cell develops a hair bundle sensitive to caudad stimulation and the posteriorly positioned sibling extends a bundle responsive to rostrad water movement.
source: Following mitosis, the newly formed sibling cells undergo a series of stereotypical rearrangements in their relative anteroposterior positions, after which the more anteriorly positioned hair cell develops a hair bundle sensitive to caudad stimulation and the posteriorly positioned sibling extends a bundle responsive to rostrad water movement.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hair cell polarity determination.

claim: Trilobite mutant larvae, in which the vangl2 protein is inactivated, possess hair bundles with random orientations.
source: Because trilobite mutant larvae, in which the vangl2 protein is inactivated, possess hair bundles with random orientations, the canonical planar-cell-polarity pathway participates in cellular patterning.
evidence: This is supported by the SBFSEM data from trilobite mutants and cited literature.

claim: The canonical planar-cell-polarity pathway participates in cellular patterning.
source: Because trilobite mutant larvae, in which the vangl2 protein is inactivated, possess hair bundles with random orientations, the canonical planar-cell-polarity pathway participates in cellular patterning.
evidence: This is inferred from the trilobite mutant phenotype and supported by literature.

claim: Each afferent neuron of the posterior lateral line receives innervation from hair cells of only one orientation through a process that requires neither mechanotransduction nor synaptic activity.
source: Finally, through a process that requires neither mechanotransduction nor synaptic activity, each afferent neuron of the posterior lateral line receives innervation from hair cells of only one orientation (Figure 1F–H; Nagiel et al., 2008; Nagiel et al., 2009; Wibowo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 1F-H and cited literature.

claim: The neural calculations necessary for rheotaxis, escape swimming, and schooling require directionally specific information from discrete populations of neurons connected to hair cells of the two polarities.
source: In addition to the linear arrangement of neuromasts along the tail, the neural calculations necessary for rheotaxis, escape swimming, and schooling require directionally specific information from discrete populations of neurons connected to hair cells of the two polarities (Oteiza et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on lateral line function in behavior.

claim: Serial blockface scanning electron microscopy (SBFSEM) has made possible the reconstruction of complete axons and dendrites within modules of the nervous system.
source: Serial blockface scanning electron microscopy (SBFSEM) has made possible the reconstruction of complete axons and dendrites within modules of the nervous system (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SBFSEM capabilities.

claim: Neuronal connections have been investigated in detail in species with very few neurons, such as roundworms, and in structures with a crystalline degree of order, such as the fruit fly's visual pathway.
source: Neuronal connections have been investigated in detail in species with very few neurons, such as roundworms, and in structures with a crystalline degree of order, such as the fruit fly's visual pathway.
evidence: This is established knowledge about connectomics research.

claim: The volumes of most structures of interest require weeks to months of specialized microscopy and tens of thousands of hours of manual segmentation to reconstruct a single specimen.
source: Although SBFSEM offers sufficient resolution to reveal the fine details of neural microcircuits in vertebrate nervous systems as well, the volumes of most structures of interest require weeks to months of specialized microscopy and tens of thousands of hours of manual segmentation to reconstruct a single specimen (Denk and Horstmann, 2004; Helmstaedter et al., 2011; Wanner et al., 2016; Hildebrand et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on SBFSEM methodology and time requirements.

claim: There are few if any SBFSEM studies in which multiple circuits have been compared between individuals or during development.
source: As a consequence, there are few if any SBFSEM studies in which multiple circuits have been compared between individuals or during development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the literature review and the novelty of the current study.

claim: Eight wild-type zebrafish neuromasts were analyzed by SBFSEM.
source: We analyzed single neuromasts from each of eight zebrafish (Figure 2A; Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and results sections.

claim: The axonal terminals associated with each neuromast entered through a single perforation in the basal lamina as branches arising from peripheral axons in the posterior lateral-line nerve.
source: The axonal terminals associated with each neuromast entered through a single perforation in the basal lamina as branches arising from peripheral axons in the posterior lateral-line nerve (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the SBFSEM data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Each SBFSEM data set included approximately 40 μm of a posterior lateral-line nerve.
source: Each SBFSEM data set included approximately 40 μm of a posterior lateral-line nerve.
evidence: This is a description of the data collection parameters.

claim: Upon examining 14 individually labeled neurons by confocal fluorescence microscopy, there were no instances of a bifurcated axon extending terminals into a neuromast.
source: Upon examining 14 individually labeled neurons by confocal fluorescence microscopy, however, we found no instances of a bifurcated axon extending terminals into a neuromast.
evidence: This is supported by the confocal microscopy data collected by the authors.

claim: Previous investigators had estimated that two to four neurons enter a neuromast.
source: Whereas previous investigators had estimated that two to four neurons enter a neuromast (Liao, 2010), we found an average of 9.3 neuronal branches in each sensory organ.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: An average of 9.3 neuronal branches enter each neuromast.
source: Whereas previous investigators had estimated that two to four neurons enter a neuromast (Liao, 2010), we found an average of 9.3 neuronal branches in each sensory organ.
evidence: This is supported by the SBFSEM data from eight wild-type specimens.

claim: The majority of neuromasts included one axonal terminal that made direct contact with every hair cell without apposition to any synaptic ribbon.
source: The majority of neuromasts included one axonal terminal that made direct contact with every hair cell without apposition to any synaptic ribbon.
evidence: This is supported by the SBFSEM data analysis.

claim: Terminals with presynaptic vesicles and postsynaptic membrane cisterns that contact every hair cell without apposition to synaptic ribbons are identified as efferent axon terminals.
source: Together with the presence of numerous presynaptic vesicles and postsynaptic membrane cisterns, this wiring pattern identified these structures as the terminals of efferent axons (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on established ultrastructural criteria for identifying efferent terminals.

claim: 16% of afferent terminals displayed minimal or no branching and tapered to termini immediately inside the neuromasts.
source: Of these terminals, 16% displayed minimal or no branching and tapered to termini immediately inside the neuromasts.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: 84% of afferent terminals occupied perisynaptic compartments.
source: The remaining 84% of the terminals occupied perisynaptic compartments, the spaces bounded by supporting cells beneath hair-cell synapses (Figure 2D); 74% displayed membrane contacts at hair-cell bases, and 59% were postsynaptic to hair cells at ribbon synapses.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: 74% of afferent terminals displayed membrane contacts at hair-cell bases.
source: The remaining 84% of the terminals occupied perisynaptic compartments, the spaces bounded by supporting cells beneath hair-cell synapses (Figure 2D); 74% displayed membrane contacts at hair-cell bases, and 59% were postsynaptic to hair cells at ribbon synapses.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: 59% of afferent terminals were postsynaptic to hair cells at ribbon synapses.
source: The remaining 84% of the terminals occupied perisynaptic compartments, the spaces bounded by supporting cells beneath hair-cell synapses (Figure 2D); 74% displayed membrane contacts at hair-cell bases, and 59% were postsynaptic to hair cells at ribbon synapses.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: Among 344 presynaptic active zones in hair cells, only four were apposed to axonal terminals of the opposite polarity preference.
source: Among 344 presynaptic active zones in hair cells, only four were apposed to axonal terminals of the opposite polarity preference.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data from wild-type specimens.

claim: 92% of the contact area between hair cells and terminals was polarity-specific.
source: Furthermore, 92% of the contact area between hair cells and terminals was polarity-specific.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: Specificity was not predominantly a result of spatial segregation, as many axonal terminals were located perisynaptically to hair cells of both polarities.
source: This specificity was not predominantly a result of spatial segregation, for many axonal terminals were located perisynaptically to hair cells of both polarities.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the spatial relationships in the SBFSEM data.

claim: In all six observed cases of young hair cells that contacted axonal terminals but had not yet developed ribbon synapses, the hair cells made predominant or exclusive contact with terminals whose innervation by neighboring mature hair cells indicated sensitivity to rostrad stimulation.
source: Moreover, specificity did not appear to arise simply by the precocious arrival of an appropriate afferent terminal at a nascent hair cell: in all six observed cases of young hair cells that contacted axonal terminals but had not yet developed ribbon synapses, the hair cells made predominant or exclusive contact with terminals whose innervation by neighboring mature hair cells indicated sensitivity to rostrad stimulation.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of nascent hair cells in the SBFSEM data.

claim: The formation of polarity-specific ribbon synapses between hair cells and afferent terminals began as soon as synaptic ribbons became apparent, with no significant change over time in the frequency with which hair cells of the opposite polarity innervated the terminals.
source: The formation of polarity-specific ribbon synapses between hair cells and afferent terminals began as soon as synaptic ribbons became apparent, with no significant change over time in the frequency with which hair cells of the opposite polarity innervated the terminals.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of hair cells at different developmental stages in the SBFSEM data.

claim: The preponderance of the contact area was occupied by polarity-appropriate axonal terminals by 5–15 hr, a bias that grew after 15 hr.
source: In addition, the preponderance of the contact area was occupied by polarity-appropriate axonal terminals by 5–15 hr, a bias that grew after 15 hr (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Specificity is mediated primarily by direct interactions between hair cells and axonal terminals.
source: By viewing the complete set of cellular interactions at ribbon synapses during different stages of synaptic development, we recognized that specificity is mediated primarily by direct interactions between hair cells and axonal terminals.
evidence: This is inferred from the SBFSEM data showing direct contacts without intervening cells.

claim: It is unlikely that a guidepost cell or other third party mediated microcircuit assembly because no other cells intervened between the nerve fibers and the synaptic regions of hair cells.
source: Because no other cells intervened between the nerve fibers and the synaptic regions of hair cells, it is unlikely that a guidepost cell or other third party mediated microcircuit assembly as has been reported in other systems (Shen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is inferred from the SBFSEM data showing direct contacts and comparison with other systems.

claim: The polarity specificity of innervation depends upon short-range cues unique to hair cells and the polarity-appropriate subset of afferent neurons.
source: This pattern suggested that the polarity specificity of innervation depends upon short-range cues unique to hair cells and the polarity-appropriate subset of afferent neurons.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of direct contacts and specificity in the SBFSEM data.

claim: The average number of synaptic partners per hair cell increased from one in cells aged 5–15 hr to two for cells older than 15 hr.
source: First, the average number of synaptic partners per hair cell increased from one in cells aged 5–15 hr to two for cells older than 15 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Each hair cell formed increasing numbers of perisynaptic relationships with other axonal terminals as it matured.
source: Second, in addition to its immediate innervation partners, each hair cell formed increasing numbers of perisynaptic relationships with other axonal terminals.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of perisynaptic associations over developmental time.

claim: Nearly equal proportions of afferent terminals of each polarity preference occupied a hair cell's perisynaptic compartment.
source: Nearly equal proportions of afferent terminals of each polarity preference occupied a hair cell's perisynaptic compartment, but of the contacting terminals that did not form ribbon synapses a greater number were of the opposing polarity.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of perisynaptic associations in the SBFSEM data.

claim: Of the contacting terminals that did not form ribbon synapses, a greater number were of the opposing polarity.
source: Nearly equal proportions of afferent terminals of each polarity preference occupied a hair cell's perisynaptic compartment, but of the contacting terminals that did not form ribbon synapses a greater number were of the opposing polarity.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of membrane contacts in the SBFSEM data.

claim: One axonal terminal occupied the majority of the hair cells' presynaptic active zones and contact area.
source: The redundant innervation by hair cells was unequally distributed: one axonal terminal occupied the majority of the hair cells' presynaptic active zones and contact area.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of synaptic dominance in the SBFSEM data.

claim: Dominance by a single terminal increased with age: the dominant terminal received 34% of the ribbon synapses and 53% of the contact area of hair cells at 5–15 hr compared to 75% of the synapses and 73% of the contact area of hair cells older than 15 hr.
source: This dominance by a single terminal increased with age: the dominant terminal received 34% of the ribbon synapses and 53% of the contact area of hair cells at 5–15 hr compared to 75% of the synapses and 73% of the contact area of hair cells older than 15 hr (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Every neuromast possessed one terminal of each polarity that accounted for more than half of the presynaptic active zones and contact area for hair cells of that polarity.
source: Furthermore, every neuromast possessed one terminal of each polarity that accounted for more than half of the presynaptic active zones and contact area for hair cells of that polarity (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Dominance is a property of the axonal terminal that leads to its participation in the majority of ribbon synapses across a majority of hair cells.
source: This pattern suggests that dominance is a property of the axonal terminal that leads to its participation in the majority of ribbon synapses across a majority of hair cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of dominance observed across multiple hair cells.

claim: Previous research has shown that lateral-line afferent neurons contact three to five consecutive neuromasts and often do so unequally.
source: Previous research has shown that lateral-line afferent neurons contact three to five consecutive neuromasts and often do so unequally, with some axonal branches ramifying extensively throughout a neuromast but other branches entering more distal or proximal neuromasts with minimal arborization (Nagiel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: The dominance of axonal terminals is a property local to particular axonal branches and the corresponding neuromasts, rather than a characteristic of an entire neuron.
source: This pattern suggests that the dominance of axonal terminals is a property local to particular axonal branches and the corresponding neuromasts, rather than a characteristic of an entire neuron.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of unequal innervation across neuromasts by single neurons.

claim: When all fibers save one have been experimentally ablated, hair cells are able to innervate neurons of the opposing polarity.
source: When all fibers save one have been experimentally ablated, hair cells are able to innervate neurons of the opposing polarity (Pujol-Martí et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on ablation experiments.

claim: There were numerous instances in which the least dominant afferent terminal specific to a given polarity of hair cell participated in a ribbon synapse despite the contiguity of the most dominant terminal of the opposing polarity.
source: Nevertheless, we encountered numerous instances in which the least dominant afferent terminal specific to a given polarity of hair cell participated in a ribbon synapse despite the contiguity of the most dominant terminal of the opposing polarity.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the SBFSEM data showing specificity overriding dominance.

claim: There were no cases in which dominance superseded specificity in innervation.
source: In support of this conclusion, there were no cases in which dominance superseded specificity in innervation, that is, in which the highest-dominance axonal terminal of the opposing polarity preference displaced the lowest-dominance terminal from a hair cell of its characteristic polarity preference.
evidence: This is supported by comprehensive analysis of all synaptic connections in the SBFSEM data.

claim: Within each polarity-specific subset of neurons, competition determines the innervation partner.
source: Within each polarity-specific subset of neurons, competition therefore determines the innervation partner.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that specificity is maintained while dominance varies within polarity-specific subsets.

claim: The microcircuitry of neuromasts is characterized by specificity, redundancy, and dominance.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that the microcircuitry of neuromasts is characterized by specificity, redundancy, and dominance.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by all the SBFSEM data presented.

claim: Polarity-specific neuronal associations begin at the earliest appearance of synaptic ribbons and increase with age.
source: Polarity-specific neuronal associations begin at the earliest appearance of synaptic ribbons and increase with age along with the dominance hierarchy of axonal terminals and the redundancy of both innervated and contacted fibers.
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis of the SBFSEM data.

claim: Each hair cell recruits a few polarity-specific neuronal partners while maintaining an extensive but loose network of diverse neuronal associations.
source: Each hair cell recruits a few polarity-specific neuronal partners while maintaining an extensive but loose network of diverse neuronal associations.
evidence: This is a summary of the redundancy and specificity patterns observed in the SBFSEM data.

claim: Four trilobite mutant neuromasts were examined by SBFSEM.
source: We first examined one neuromast in each of four trilobite mutant larvae, in which inactivation of the canonical planar-cell-polarity protein vangl2 causes hair bundles to orient randomly (Hammerschmidt et al., 1996; López-Schier and Hudspeth, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and results sections.

claim: In trilobite mutants, 73% of ribbons were partnered with terminals that were innervated both by hair cells that completed rearrangement anterior to their siblings and by those that assumed posterior positions.
source: By this criterion, axonal terminals of mutants did not show the normal pattern of discrimination: 73% of ribbons were partnered with terminals that were innervated both by hair cells that completed rearrangement anterior to their siblings and by those that assumed posterior positions (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Figure 5—source data 1; Video 3).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the trilobite mutant SBFSEM data.

claim: When innervation was compared between sibling hair cells in trilobite mutants, afferent terminals were almost perfectly innervated by only one hair cell per sibling pair; only one synaptic ribbon of 101 was apposed to an axonal terminal that also contacted the sibling hair cell.
source: Indeed, when innervation was compared between sibling hair cells, we found that afferent terminals were almost perfectly innervated by only one hair cell per sibling pair; only one synaptic ribbon of 101 was apposed to an axonal terminal that also contacted the sibling hair cell.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of sibling pairs in the trilobite mutant SBFSEM data.

claim: In trilobite mutants, the more anterior or more posterior sibling did not preferentially innervate the terminals, indicating that the two chemical identities appeared to have been distributed randomly.
source: Because the more anterior or more posterior sibling did not preferentially innervate the terminals, the two chemical identities appeared to have been distributed randomly.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of sibling innervation patterns in trilobite mutants.

claim: In the absence of canonical planar-cell-polarity signaling, the distinct cellular identity of each sibling that determines polarity-specific innervation is nevertheless uniquely allocated.
source: This pattern indicates that, in the absence of canonical planar-cell-polarity signaling, the distinct cellular identity of each sibling that determines polarity-specific innervation is nevertheless uniquely allocated.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that siblings maintain distinct innervation despite random positioning in trilobite mutants.

claim: In trilobite mutants, unlike wild-type specimens, the siblings of a common cellular identity were randomly arranged with respect to their anterior-posterior position.
source: However, unlike the hair cells of wild-type specimens, the siblings of a common cellular identity were randomly arranged with respect to their anterior-posterior position.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of sibling positioning in trilobite mutant SBFSEM data.

claim: Apart from specificity, trilobite mutant specimens showed redundant innervation and a distribution of afferent-terminal dominance similar to that of normal larvae.
source: Apart from specificity, the remainder of the trilobite microcircuitry remained intact: mutant specimens showed redundant innervation and a distribution of afferent-terminal dominance similar to that of normal larvae.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative comparison of trilobite and wild-type SBFSEM data.

claim: Previous research had shown that activity is not necessary for polarity-specific innervation.
source: Previous research had shown that activity is not necessary for polarity-specific innervation, a rebuttal to the proposition that axonal terminals achieve specificity by detecting coincident depolarization of hair cells (Nagiel et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: Among 14 neurons in trilobite mutants that were innervated by more than one hair cell, each eschewed the formation of synapses with hair cells with a similar vector of mechanosensitivity in favor of those with dissimilar or even opposite orientations.
source: We used preimaging with confocal fluorescence microscopy and subsequent SBFSEM to evaluate 14 neurons that were innervated by more than one hair cell. Each eschewed the formation of synapses with hair cells with a similar vector of mechanosensitivity in favor of those with dissimilar or even opposite orientations.
evidence: This is supported by combined confocal and SBFSEM analysis of trilobite mutants.

claim: Synaptic activity is neither necessary nor sufficient to instruct polarity-specific innervation.
source: Synaptic activity is therefore neither necessary nor sufficient to instruct polarity-specific innervation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that neurons in trilobite mutants do not preferentially innervate hair cells with similar mechanosensitivity.

claim: Notch signaling is active in the neuromast and appears to regulate the entry of supporting cells into mitosis to create new hair cells.
source: Notch signaling is also active in the neuromast and appears to regulate the entry of supporting cells into mitosis to create new hair cells (Haddon et al., 1998; Wibowo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on Notch signaling in the neuromast.

claim: Previous work suggested that Notch signaling plays a role in the polarization of hair cells, as disruption of the pathway with the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT results in a biased distribution of hair-bundle polarizations.
source: Previous work suggested that Notch signaling also plays a role in the polarization of hair cells, for disruption of the pathway with the γ-secretase inhibitor DAPT results in a biased distribution of hair-bundle polarizations (Mirkovic et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited literature on Notch signaling and hair cell polarity.

claim: All the hair cells in Notch-overexpressing larvae possessed anteriorly polarized hair bundles.
source: All the hair cells in these larvae possessed anteriorly polarized hair bundles.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of Notch-overexpressing larvae by SBFSEM and confocal microscopy.

claim: Two Notch-overexpressing neuromasts were investigated by SBFSEM.
source: We investigated by SBFSEM one mutant specimen from each of two animals (Figure 6; Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Figure 6—source data 1; Video 4).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and results sections.

claim: In Notch-overexpressing mutants, 93% of presynaptic active zones were partnered with afferent terminals that were innervated by both anteriorly and posteriorly positioned hair cells.
source: Grouping the hair cells by their anteroposterior positions after rearrangement revealed that 93% of presynaptic active zones were partnered with afferent terminals that were innervated by both anteriorly and posteriorly positioned hair cells.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of the Notch-overexpressing mutant SBFSEM data.

claim: When hair cells in Notch-overexpressing mutants were analyzed as sibling pairs, in every instance both cells innervated a common axonal terminal.
source: Furthermore, when hair cells were analyzed as sibling pairs, in every instance both cells innervated a common axonal terminal.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of sibling pairs in the Notch-overexpressing mutant SBFSEM data.

claim: In the absence of normal Notch signaling, the unique chemical identities mediating innervation apparently failed to be asymmetrically allotted to each sibling; instead, the same identity was possessed by both.
source: In the absence of normal Notch signaling, the unique chemical identities mediating innervation apparently failed to be asymmetrically allotted to each sibling; instead, the same identity was possessed by both.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both siblings innervate the same terminals in Notch-overexpressing mutants.

claim: The wiring and miswiring of neuromasts was characterized at 3–4 dpf, so any subsequent alterations in wiring during the late larval, juvenile, or adult stages would have gone undetected.
source: Because we characterized the wiring and miswiring of neuromasts at 3–4 dpf, any subsequent alterations in wiring during the late larval, juvenile, or adult stages would have gone undetected.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors regarding the developmental time window studied.

claim: Like the trilobite specimens, the Notch-overexpressing mutants retained the wild-type microcircuit characteristics of redundancy and dominance even though the specificity of innervation had been eliminated.
